title: Check sign-in methods, password reset readiness and Temporary Access Passes before admins move to phishing-resistant sign-in
situation: Larkspur Example Health (fictional) wants every administrator and clinician to sign in with phishing-resistant methods. Before the Conditional Access policies are switched from report-only to on, the identity team exported the authentication methods policy, a custom authentication strength for the finance app, 15 recent sign-in attempts, the self-service password reset (SSPR) settings for 10 users and 8 Temporary Access Pass (TAP) requests from the help desk.
your_task: For each sign-in, check whether the method is enabled for the user's groups in the authentication methods policy, including group exclusions and the Microsoft Authenticator mode.
Check whether the method satisfies the authentication strength the Conditional Access policy requires, and list the methods that would satisfy it.
Decide whether each user can reset their own password: count only methods SSPR accepts, and apply the stricter administrator policy to anyone holding an admin role.
Accept or reject each Temporary Access Pass against the tenant's lifetime limits and one-time-use rule.
why_it_matters: Attackers now use fake sign-in pages that relay SMS codes and push approvals in real time. Only phishing-resistant methods stop that, and a rollout fails if users have no enabled method that meets the new strength, cannot reset a password, or receive long-lived reusable passes that work like a second password.
done_when: Every sign-in is marked SATISFIED, NOT_SATISFIED or METHOD_DISABLED, with the reason and the methods that would work.
Every user is marked SSPR_READY, NOT_REGISTERED, INSUFFICIENT_METHODS or ADMIN_POLICY.
Every Temporary Access Pass request is marked TAP_VALID or TAP_REJECTED with the policy rule it broke.

glossary.Authentication methods policy: The Microsoft Entra ID setting that turns each sign-in method on or off and targets it at groups; an excluded group always loses the method.
glossary.Authentication strength: A Conditional Access grant control that lists which method combinations may satisfy a sign-in, such as Multifactor authentication (MFA), Passwordless MFA or Phishing-resistant MFA.
glossary.Conditional Access (CA): Microsoft Entra ID's policy engine that decides, per sign-in, whether to allow, block or demand stronger proof.
glossary.Phishing-resistant MFA: Methods tied to the real website by public-key cryptography, so a fake page cannot reuse them: passkeys (FIDO2), Windows Hello for Business and multifactor certificate-based authentication (CBA).
glossary.FIDO2 and AAGUID: FIDO2 is the open standard behind passkeys; the Authenticator Attestation GUID (AAGUID) identifies the make and model of a security key so a policy can allow only approved models.
glossary.Self-service password reset (SSPR): Lets users reset their own password after proving who they are with a set number of registered methods.
glossary.Temporary Access Pass (TAP): A time-limited passcode an administrator issues so a user can sign in and register passwordless methods.

talking_point: Checked 15 sign-ins against Conditional Access authentication strengths (4 satisfied, 7 not satisfied, 4 blocked because the method was not enabled for the user), found 6 of 10 users not ready for self-service password reset (3 with nothing usable registered, 2 with too few methods and 1 administrator short of the two-method admin rule), and rejected 6 of 8 Temporary Access Pass requests for breaking the lifetime, expiry, one-time-use or group-targeting rules.
